candidates.label: AnalysisNewsArticle
candidates.comment: An AnalysisNewsArticle is a NewsArticle that combines factual reporting with the author's expertise, offering interpretations and conclusions. Also called news analysis, interpretive news, expert commentary. Examples: An article analyzing the economic impact of a new policy, a piece interpreting election results, a report on scientific findings with expert commentary. Distinct from NewsArticle, which primarily focuses on factual reporting without extensive interpretation.

candidates.label: ReviewNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A specialized news article that combines factual reporting with a professional critic's assessment of a service, product, performance, or artistic work. Also called critical news report, professional review article, news critique. Examples: a New York Times review of a Broadway show, a tech blog's assessment of a new smartphone, a music magazine's album critique.

candidates.label: Comment
candidates.comment: A textual remark or observation made about an item, such as a blog post. Also called remark, feedback, note, annotation. Examples: A user's comment on a YouTube video, a review on a product page, a blog post comment, a code comment.

candidates.label: SatiricalArticle
candidates.comment: An article whose content is primarily satirical, meaning it uses humor, irony, exaggeration, or ridicule to expose and criticize people's stupidity or vices, and is not intended to be literally true. Also called parody article, spoof news, humorous critique, ironic commentary. Examples: an article from The Onion, a piece from a satirical magazine, a political cartoon with extensive text. Distinct from NewsArticle, which aims to report factual information.

candidates.label: MediaReview
candidates.comment: A specialized review dedicated to evaluating online media content, often in the context of fact-checking and misinformation. Also called media fact-check, content authenticity review, misinformation analysis. Examples: a fact-check of a viral video, an analysis of a manipulated image, a review of a misleading news article. Distinct from Review, which is a general evaluation of any item or service.

candidates.label: StatisticalPopulation
candidates.comment: A set of instances of a given type that satisfy specific constraints, used for statistical analysis. Also called statistical group, data population, sample group, target demographic. Examples: all persons with a home location in a specific city, all events occurring in a particular year, all news articles mentioning a certain keyword. Distinct from StatisticalVariable, which represents a measurable metric within a population.

candidates.label: StatisticalVariable
candidates.comment: A measurable statistical metric that can be observed at a place and time, defined by a population type and specific constraints. Also called statistical metric, data point, observable quantity, measurement variable. Examples: median height of female persons, average temperature in a city, count of news articles published daily. Distinct from StatisticalPopulation, which is the group being measured, not the measurement itself.
